newsitem.title: USA: US Midwest direct hogs seen flat-$0.50 lower-trade.
newsitem.headline: US Midwest direct hogs seen flat-$0.50 lower-trade.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog prices Wednesday were seen steady to $0.50 per cwt lower, pressured by hefty hog marketings on Tuesday and expectations for continued big receipts Wednesday, dealers said.

Cold, damp weather in the Corn Belt kept producers away from preparing fields for planting and freed them up to market more hogs, they said. Producers try to market as many hogs as they can anyway to stay current before spring planting gets underway in full force by mid-April, the dealers said.
Interior Iowa/southern Minnesota hog marketing estimates Tuesday were 110,000 head, USDA reported.
Interior Iowa and southern Minnesota top prices for hogs delivered to the plant could range $52.50 to $53.00, the dealers said.
Illinois top prices for hogs to the plant could range $52.00 to $52.50. Indiana/Ohio top prices for delivered hogs to the plant could span $51.50 to $52.00, they said.
Weakness in cash hog prices also were expected from soft pork prices on Tuesday, dealers said.
Fresh pork prices at midday Tuesday were quoted steady for hams and down $2.00 to $4.00 per cwt for pork bellies in slow trading, USDA reported.
